minutes.headline: Commission approved a 5-year plan to hand-harvest and chemically treat invasive weeds at Lake Wham's town beach.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard several wetlands notices of intent and requests for determination, approving driveway, septic, deck, wall and tree-removal projects in buffer zones, and continuing two hearings (68A Laurel Lane for a missing NOI number, and a Tanner Cole common driveway pending peer review) to September 3rd. The most significant action was approval of a five-year order of conditions for the town's Lake Wham aquatic plant and algae management program using hand/diver-assisted harvesting and herbicides near the public beach, conditioned on an annual report. Two certificates of compliance and one tree-removal request were left unresolved pending agent follow-up or a site visit.

public_comment.topic: Raised concerns about the Chaplain driveway easement width, a drain pipe crossing, and an existing town catch basin that floods at the bottom of the driveway.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 91 Main Street, former parks commissioner
public_comment.topic: Spoke in support of the Lake Wham weed treatment plan, comparing it to Lake Shirley's practice and stressing swimmer safety.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 362 Sunset Lane, lives on Lake Shirley
public_comment.topic: Described how Lake Shirley fully closes for herbicide treatment days and asked whether Lake Wham could do the same and how residents would be notified.

budget_items.topic: Lake Wham aquatic plant management costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said diver-assisted suction harvesting is significantly more expensive than plain hand harvesting, so the plan is to hand-harvest first and use herbicides only as needed to control costs to taxpayers.

budget_items.topic: Lake Wham 5-year order of conditions request
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said requesting a five-year order (instead of the usual three) was mainly to avoid repeatedly paying a consultant to appear before the commission.

budget_items.topic: Abutter notification for Lake Wham herbicide treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant said mailing a certified abutters list would add another cost each time, and preferred relying on the town website and social media instead.
The chair said Massachusetts Association of Conservation Commissions classes and the fall convention are covered under the commission's existing budget and encouraged members to attend.
The chair said the committee is moving to a different consultant to move the stormwater utility program forward, hoping to present something in the fall.

decisions.decision: Applicant for 68A Laurel Lane will try to resolve the missing NOI/D number before returning for the September 3rd meeting.
The certificate of compliance for 701 Reservoir Road was held pending the conservation agent's response; the chair will message the administrator and follow up with the applicant.
The certificate of compliance for 155 Reservoir Road will be added to the next meeting's agenda since neither the applicant nor the agent's notes were available.
The tree-removal request for 44 Hemlock Terrace will go on the September 3rd agenda after a site visit is completed beforehand.
Commission members were invited to sign up for a September 19th half-day trail work event at the Cry Nature Center as part of the United Way Day of Caring.

The commission will set aside dedicated time on a future agenda, rather than discuss informally, to go over the master plan steering committee feedback spreadsheet since a quorum discussing it would require an open meeting.
The chair will add a 6:30 p.m. executive session to the September 3rd agenda to discuss the Hollis Road property.

what_happened.line: The Commission approved a five-year order of conditions for the town's Lake Wham aquatic plant and algae management program, hand-harvesting and using herbicides near the public beach, with an annual report required.
The plan favors hand-harvesting over costlier diver-assisted suction and relies on the town website and social media rather than mailed abutter notice ahead of herbicide treatments.
Two hearings were continued to September 3: Ashley Owens's 68A Laurel Lane project, missing its NOI number, and Tanner Cole's common driveway, pending peer review.
The Commission also approved several driveway, septic, wall, deck and tree-removal projects in wetland buffer zones, and issued negative determinations for a well and a deck project.
Two certificates of compliance and one tree-removal request were left unresolved, pending agent follow-up or a site visit before the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The Lake Wham approval sets a five-year plan for herbicide use near the town beach, with notice to residents handled through the town website and social media rather than a mailed abutter list.
Wetland buffer-zone approvals for driveways, septic systems, walls and tree removal show how the Commission conditions rather than blocks routine residential projects near water.
Two properties (68A Laurel Lane, Tanner Cole's driveway) and two certificates of compliance remain undecided, affecting those owners' pending work.
